processAdapter.host: One owned Electron utilityProcess per engine, Node fork outside Electron; RTC addon never loaded in Main. Same native ABI, codecs, routing and clock domains.
processAdapter.submitEncodedFrame: Promise of the actual child native-copy receipt; admission is not processing retirement. LiveSenderFlow retains one original AU in the bounded capture pipe until acknowledgement, then consumes that exact receipt without resubmission.
processAdapter.faults: ERR_RTC_HOST_EXIT rejects pending work after owned OS process exit. Native byte ownership can then retire; external Chromium texture references remain owned until their independent retirement proof.

commands.source.createEncodedVideo: target=0; {width:even[2,3840],height:even[2,2160],fps:integer[1,120],syncGroup,enabled?:false} -> {sourceId}; requires engine videoInput:'encoded-h264'. Each independently encoded rendition owns its engine and external video source. RTC cannot rescale or increase the source framerate; no GPU/raw input import or transmitter codec instantiation.
commands.peer.configureBitrate: target=peerId; {startBitrateBps,maxBitrateBps},150000<=start<=max<=80000000. Public PeerConnection.SetBitrate only once before publication; no forced minimum or periodic estimator resets. Returns configured values plus minimumBitrateForced:false and bandwidthMeasured:false. This is a startup estimate, not proof of available bandwidth; congestion control remains responsible for later allocation.
commands.peer.configureVideoPlayout: target=peerId; {minimumDelayMs:integer[0,1000]}, only once before any receivers exist. Applies the public SetJitterBufferMinimumDelay API to video receivers; audio is unchanged. Returns {minimumDelayMs,actualDelayMeasured:false}; a request is not an end-to-end latency measurement.

node.options: Revision6 options plus videoInput:'nv12'|'encoded-h264' (default nv12). Encoded source and engine modes must match.
node.submitEncodedFrame: engine.submitEncodedFrame(sourceId,{frameId,data:Buffer,keyframe,timestampUs,durationUs,ntpTimeMs,pts,dts,timebaseNumerator,timebaseDenominator}) -> {sourceId,frameId,inputBytes,copied:true,networkDeliveryConfirmed:false}; synchronous bounded native copy, not a JS-memory loan, retirement Promise or network delivery proof. PTS/DTS are original canonical signed int64 decimal strings.

events.source.encodedFrameReleased: target=sourceId; {sourceId,frameId,acceptedCodecCallbacks,explicitlyNotSent,cancelled,unconsumed,pausedConsumerPresent,nativeCopyRetired:true,networkDeliveryConfirmed:false}; final native compressed copy retirement, not remote delivery.
events.source.encodedFeedback: target=sourceId; sequence increases at actual event delivery. kind:'rate'|'encoder-closed' exposes requestedBitrateBps, selected bitrateBps, requestedFps, fpsApplied:null, paused and80Mbps ceiling. kind:'keyframe' requests next-real-idr (one keyint_sec=1 GOP; maximumWaitMs:1500 is the nominal wait at the configured rate). kind:'recovery' carries frameId,generation,reason:'rtc-unconsumed'|'input-expired'|'publication-expired'|'codec-expired'|'clock-sample-uncertain',mode:'next-real-idr',maximumWaitMs:1500 and keyframeConfirmed:false; it invalidates dependent queued pictures without fabricating ownership retirement or bypassing congestion control.

input.codec: Annex B H264 Main, maximum level6; negotiate at least5.1 for1080p120/4K30,5.2 for4K60 and6 for4K120. Exact source dimensions, BT.709 limited, L1T1; no B slices. A smaller rendition may carry a lower valid H264 level; actual SPS cannot exceed the negotiated level. Current in-band SPS/PPS are retained transactionally and completed on IDR; no stale extra-data reinsertion. Source stats expose the actual SPS profileLevelId only after observing it.
input.timestamps: timestampUs is the genuine original presentation time in system-QPC microseconds, mapped by the existing paired capture clock. Frame IDs, timestamps and original PTS/DTS each increase strictly. Independent DTS offset is valid with I/P pictures; neither timestamp is synthesized from packet index or rewritten to equal the other. ntpTimeMs=-1 when unavailable.
input.bounds: 4MiB per AU,16 retained native copies/8MiB total, maximum input age500ms including the codec boundary. Only one RTC frame-buffer dispatch is outstanding; its retirement detects unconsumed pictures and fences their dependency generation before dispatching another. A dispatch still outstanding after 500ms fences the stale queued dependencies and resumes through the next real IDR; only a dispatch held for 5s fails the source. Expired AUs are never forwarded. Input rejected for IDR recovery throws ERR_RTC_ENCODED_RECOVERY with BUSY(status8), without admitting a copy; other errors remain failures. Recovery is bounded in encoded AUs, not wall time: three configured-rate GOPs (3 x fps AUs), so an encoder that skips frames under CPU load cannot end the share. The bound is preserved across repeated failed IDRs and recovery completes only when a current IDR is actually accepted by the codec callback. Closed, disabled, paused or no-consumer sources reject admission explicitly.
input.feedback: A shared encoder uses the lowest positive requested bitrate across active consumers, capped at80Mbps and by the selected source profile. All-zero feedback pauses admission; resume waits for a real IDR. requestedFps is the finite uint32-domain RTC arrival-rate estimate, which can exceed the120fps media configuration during bursts; it never retimes media or claims applied FPS. Encoded-only factories keep the350ms congestion window and30Kbps pushback floor, but lower producer bitrate instead of raw-frame dropping. Overshoot adjustment, pacing and congestion control remain active; NV12 factories retain their defaults.
input.ownership: Source shutdown fences publication and joins its worker only after every native encoded buffer has retired. GPU receiver leases retain the existing external-reference/fence proof; encoded bytes never replace those obligations.

proofLimits: Compiled capabilities and CPU contracts do not qualify hardware execution, frame uniqueness, internet performance or physical presentation.
Encoded output callbacks and packet counts do not prove equal numbers of distinct captured images.
No transmitter decoding, raw conversion, scaling or second encoder is permitted.
